identity.title: Focus and Dilution: The Multi-stage Learning Process of Attention

problem.claim: The work examines training dynamics in Transformer-based models, focusing on how attention learning evolves over time.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies limited understanding of Transformer training dynamics as the motivating gap.

contributions.claim: Identifies a recurrent focus–dilution cycle in attention learning and analyzes it in a one-layer Transformer with Markovian data using gradient-flow analysis.
Decomposes one focus–dilution cycle into distinct stages through stage-wise linearization around critical points.
Characterizes how parameter freezing, frequency-driven focus, embedding perturbations, mass redistribution, and symmetry breaking form the cycle.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present the focus–dilution cycle and its staged theoretical explanation as the work's contribution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, in their analyzed setting, embedding and projection rapidly become rank-one while attention parameters remain effectively frozen, followed by attention growth toward high-frequency tokens.

The authors report that evolving attention induces embedding perturbations that progressively redistribute mass and dilute the focus; low-frequency-token asymmetries then open new embedding directions and initiate another cycle.
The authors report that experiments on synthetic Markovian data, WikiText, and TinyStories corroborate the predicted stages and cyclical dynamics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer success contrasts with limited understanding of training dynamics.
The authors identify a recurrent focus–dilution cycle and analyze it theoretically in a one-layer Markovian setting.
Stage-wise linearization separates the cycle into distinct phases.
The phases progress from rank-one condensation and frozen attention, to frequency-driven focus, dilution through embedding perturbations, and symmetry-breaking restart.
Experiments across synthetic Markovian data, WikiText, and TinyStories are reported to align with the predicted dynamics.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a high-level cyclical claim with an ordered mechanistic decomposition and then names datasets used to corroborate the stages.

lessons.interpretation: A staged mechanism can make a complex training-dynamics claim more inspectable and connect theory to targeted empirical checks.
lessons.application: For a dynamics paper, define the global cycle, partition it into observable phases, and report evidence separately for each phase.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the phenomenon has no meaningful temporal stages or when phase boundaries cannot be operationalized.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative details about rates, parameter regimes, approximation error, or the strength of the reported corroboration.
The theoretical scope is limited in the abstract to a one-layer Transformer with Markovian data; broader architectural and data-distribution applicability is unspecified.
The abstract does not state whether the cycle is claimed to be universal or only established for the analyzed setting.
